meal.title: Priority Queue in Process Scheduling
meal.objective: Describe why a priority queue is needed to order ready processes

voice.script: Why does your phone sometimes feel faster than other apps? How does the system decide which process runs next? When many processes are ready, the scheduler needs a way to pick the most important one first. A priority queue orders processes by importance. It works like a line where each person has a number, and the smallest number goes first. Here is a tiny program that uses a priority queue to pick the next process. It creates a list of (priority, name) pairs, adds them to the queue, and then removes them one by one, printing the name each time. Running it shows the highest priority process runs first. The diagram shows processes entering the queue and leaving in priority order. Remember: a priority queue lets the scheduler pick the most important ready process. Try changing the priorities and see how the order changes.

A priority queue orders processes by importance.

visual.code:
import heapq

processes = [(2, "browser"), (1, "music"), (3, "game")]
queue = []
for p in processes:
    heapq.heappush(queue, p)
while queue:
    priority, name = heapq.heappop(queue)
    print(name)
